title: beIN Sports hiring Kaylyn Kyle from MLS as lead soccer presenter after Richard Keys’ exit
content:
The Qatar-based beIN Sports has hired former Canada international Kaylyn Kyle as its new lead presenter of English-language soccer coverage, replacing Richard Keys who exited at the end of the 2025-26 season.

Kyle worked most recently for four years as a broadcaster for Major League Soccer coverage on Apple TV, but blends experience as a presenter with a noteworthy prior playing career, having represented Canada at two World Cups and winning a bronze medal at the Olympic Games in London in 2012. She previously worked for beIN on its English-language coverage of the Qatar men’s World Cup in 2022.

She now returns to beIN in a new role, executive presenter, which will be announced this week ahead of her expected first appearance to present the Premier League game between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Kyle will present football, including the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, on the network’s coverage across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).

Keys, a 69-year-old English broadcaster, and his long-term sidekick Andy Gray, a 70-year-old former Scotland international forward, left beIN this summer after 13 years in Doha.

They were previously synonymous with Sky Sports’ football coverage for the first two decades of the Premier League, which was founded in 1992.

Their careers in British television were curtailed in 2011, when Gray was sacked after making sexist remarks about assistant referee Sian Massey, while Keys resigned after clips of his part in the scandal became public.

After departing beIN, they have launched a new podcast and YouTube show called Keys and Gray Unleashed.
